depth: The depth map depicts an outdoor yard bordered on the left by a brick building wall with recessed windows and a black box on the ground about 1.5–2 m away. Grass extends forward, while trees and a white minivan appear dark in the distant right background, more than 8–10 m away. In the bright-white lower foreground, within arm’s reach at approximately 0.4–1.0 m, a small child stands in or next to a rectangular plastic tub. A white cloth at the bottom-left and, in frame 5, the camera wearer’s hand holding a blue bowl or scoop at the bottom-right lie even nearer to the lens, around 0.3–0.5 m away. Through the five frames, the camera angles slightly left and downward while the child moves from the bottom-center inside the tub—facing away/left in frame 1 and dipping mostly out of sight in frames 2–3—to the tub’s right side in frames 4–5, about 0.7–1.0 m away and roughly 0.2 m from its rim. There, the child faces away toward the building, and the wearer’s hand and bowl partly obscure the child’s lower right side in frame 5. Compared with RGB alone, the map reveals the continuous ground-plane gradient, recessed window-frame depth, and sharp foreground separation of the child’s head and shoulders from the lawn behind more clearly. It remains unreliable in the saturated white foreground, where the child’s head, tub rim, and overlapping hand/bowl in frame 5 lose internal depth contrast, and at the reflective glass windows, which look artificially deeper than the adjacent brick wall.
segmentation: Against a black background, the instance-segmentation map separates detected foreground and background items. It identifies the child as a ‘person’ near the bottom, about 0.5–1.0 m away, and the white minivan as a ‘car’ on the right, more than 10 m away and approximately 9–10 m behind the child. In frame 5, it also detects the camera wearer’s hand as a ‘person’ and the blue plastic container as a ‘frisbee’ in the bottom-right at roughly 0.3–0.5 m. During frames 1–2, only the child’s head and right hand grasping the tub rim appear at the bottom-left and bottom-center, while the minivan is partly cut off by the right edge. The child’s head sinks low enough to go completely undetected in frame 3. In frames 4–5, the child reappears standing to the right of the tub with their back toward the camera wearer; the wearer’s hand and blue container enter from the lower right and partly cover the child’s right arm and torso. The map successfully follows the small, partially cropped background car along the far-right boundary in frames 3–4 and distinguishes the overlapping wearer’s hand, blue container, and child in frame 5, although these merge visually at the RGB frame edge. Nevertheless, several results are highly unreliable: every frame omits the plastic tub, white cloth, black utility box, and building; frame 3 misses the child’s head; frame 5 wrongly calls the blue bowl/scoop a ‘frisbee’; and frame 4 invents a lime-green ‘person’ mask across the background grass and trees.
pose: The pose map contains just one detection, located at the bottom-left of frame 1 approximately 0.5–0.8 m away, within the camera wearer’s reach and close to the tub rim; frames 2–5 are entirely black. In the first frame, a tight group of yellow body keypoints indicates the child’s head and neck orientation, showing them facing away and slightly right toward the lawn rather than looking at the camera wearer. A magenta hand skeleton depicts the child’s right hand gripping the plastic tub’s upper edge just right of and slightly below the head, with about 0.15 m between them. The tub and the lower frame boundary conceal the child’s torso and legs. This skeletal overlay identifies the precise finger-joint arrangement of the child’s right hand on the rim and establishes the frame-1 head direction more clearly than the blurred head in RGB. Across the full sequence, however, the pose map is extremely unreliable: it does not detect the child’s head in frames 2–3, entirely misses the clearly visible head, back, shoulders, and left arm in frames 4–5 after the child moves to the tub’s right, and also fails to detect the camera wearer’s right hand entering the bottom-right of frame 5.
